info.title: Hevo Public API
info.description: HTTP APIs to interact with Hevo.

get.description: Retrieves details of all Destinations in your team, including their identifier, name, connector, status, and configuration settings. Credentials in the configuration settings are masked. The Destinations are ordered by `id`. A Destination that you have deleted, or that is being deleted, is not listed. The response lists only the Destinations in the region of the base URL that you call.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value used to retrieve the next set of results. Provide the `next_cursor` value returned in the previous API response.

400.description:
The request is not valid. This occurs when:

- The `limit` value is not an integer, or is outside the range of 1 to 500.
- The `cursor` value is not Base64, or does not decode to a number. Always send back the `next_cursor` value from the previous response, because a cursor that this endpoint did not return can give unexpected results instead of an error.

post.description:
Creates a Destination with the configuration settings that you provide. The settings that a Destination accepts depend on its connector. Call the [Get Configuration Details of a Destination Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-destinations-connectors-connector-id) endpoint to read the JSON schema of the request body, which states every `config` key, its data type, and whether and when it is required.

Hevo tests the connection before saving the Destination, and the call returns only after that test finishes. If Hevo cannot connect to the Destination, the request returns a `400` that includes the message from the connector, and the Destination is not created.

Read [Creating Destinations with Hevo API](/reference/creating-destinations-with-hevo-api) for the steps to create a Destination.

name.description: Unique name for your Destination, not exceeding 255 characters. The name must start with a letter or a digit, and can contain only letters, digits, spaces, hyphens (-) and underscores (_). Hevo removes any leading and trailing spaces before it checks the name. The name must be unique across your team, including the Destinations in other regions that this endpoint does not list. You can reuse the name of a Destination that you have deleted.

connector_id.description: Unique identifier of the connector that you want to use for this Destination. Retrieve this value from the [List All Destination Connectors](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-destinations-connectors) endpoint. Send this value exactly as that endpoint returns it.

type.description: (Optional) Type of the Destination. If you send this value, it must identify the same connector as the `connector_id` value.

config.description: Configuration settings for the Destination. Credentials are accepted here and are masked in every response. Read the settings that your connector accepts from the [Get Configuration Details of a Destination Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-destinations-connectors-connector-id) endpoint. Refer to [Creating Destinations with Hevo API](/reference/creating-destinations-with-hevo-api) for more information about the settings of each Destination.

400.description:
The Destination could not be created. This occurs when:

- `name` or `config` is missing.
- The `name` value is not valid, or another Destination already uses it.
- The `connector_id` value is not valid, or the `type` value does not match it.
- A `config` key fails validation.
- The connection test fails.
- The connector is in beta and has not been enabled for your team.

403.description: You do not have the permission to create a Destination. Ask your team administrator for a role that allows it.

500.description: Hevo could not complete the request. If the connection test is still running after five minutes, nothing is created. If Hevo saves the Destination but its setup then fails, the Destination is left in the `FAILED` status. Delete it and create it again. The response returns an `error_reference_id` value that you can quote to Hevo Support.

delete.description:
Deletes the Destination for the specified `destination_id`. Once deleted, a Destination cannot be restored, and Hevo also deletes every Pipeline that replicates data into it, along with the Sources that those Pipelines were created with. The tables in your Destination are not deleted. Drop them yourself if you no longer need the data.

If any Pipeline replicates data into the Destination, the request returns a `409` listing those Pipelines, unless you set the `confirm_override` query parameter to `true`. If no Pipeline replicates data into the Destination, Hevo deletes it without asking for confirmation.

Deletion does not complete immediately. The response returns the Destination in status `DELETING`. Once the request is accepted, the Destination is no longer visible through the API, and retrieving or deleting it again returns a `404`.

Refer to [Deleting a Destination](/reference/deleting-a-destination#deleting-the-destination) for more information about what is deleted along with the Destination.

patch.description:
Updates the Destination configuration for the specified `destination_id`. The available settings depend on the Destination type. To retrieve the settings that your Destination currently uses, call the [Get Details of a Destination](/reference/get_api-v2-destinations-destination-id) endpoint. To retrieve every setting that the connector accepts, along with its data type and whether it is required, call the [Get Configuration Details of a Destination Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-destinations-connectors-connector-id) endpoint.

In the request body, send only the values that you want to change. Hevo keeps the current value of every field and `config` key that you do not send. When you change the configuration settings, Hevo tests the connection before it saves the change, and the call returns once the test finishes. If the test fails, the request returns a `400` and nothing is saved. A change to only the name is saved without a connection test. Leave out the credentials that you do not want to change. If you send back the masked value (********) that a read returns for a credential, Hevo tests the connection with that value, so the test fails and the request returns a `400`.

**Note:** If you cannot send a `PATCH` request, send the same request body to the [Modify Destination Configuration (POST)](/reference/post_api-v2-destinations-destination-id) endpoint.

Refer to [Modifying a Destination](/reference/modifying-the-destination-configuration#modifying-a-destination) for more information about which settings you can change and how the change is applied.

get.description:
Retrieves the Destination connectors available to your team, including their identifier, type, name, description, and documentation link. The connectors are ordered by `connector_id`.

Use the `connector_id` value returned in this response to call the [Get Configuration Details of a Destination Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-destinations-connectors-connector-id) endpoint and retrieve the configuration settings that the connector accepts. Connectors that your team does not have access to are not listed. A connector in beta is listed only if it has been enabled for your team. The list is also limited to the Destination types that your Hevo region supports, so it can differ between regions.

Read [Find the Destination Connector](/reference/creating-destinations-with-hevo-api#step-1-find-the-destination-connector) for the steps to find the connector for your Destination.

get.summary: Get Configuration Details of a Destination Connector
get.description: Retrieves the configuration settings that a Destination connector accepts, including their data type, whether they are required, their default value, and the values they allow. Hevo returns these settings as a JSON schema draft 2020-12 definition, in which the settings specific to the connector are grouped under `config`. Use this schema to build the request body that you send to the [Create a Destination](/reference/post_api-v2-destinations) endpoint or in the `destination` object that you send to the [Create a Pipeline](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines) endpoint, or to validate it before you send the request. The schema states the following: - A key listed under `required` must always be sent. A key that Hevo fills with a default value when it is not sent is not required. - A key that applies only under a condition, such as the credentials of a specific authentication method, is defined in an `if`/`then` block inside `allOf`, and is required only when that condition is met. - A credential is a string marked `writeOnly: true` and `format: password`. Credentials are accepted while creating a Destination, or when you modify it, and are masked in every response. - A key that accepts a fixed set of values is defined as a `oneOf` list of `const` values, each with its display name in `title`. - If the value of a key must be in a particular format, the key is defined with a `pattern`, which is a regular expression that the value must match. Hevo rejects a value that does not match it. Refer to [Read the Connector Configuration](/reference/creating-destinations-with-hevo-api#step-1-read-the-connector-configuration) for more information about how to read this schema and build a request from it.

200.description: Configuration details for the connector retrieved successfully.

404.description: No connector exists with the specified `connector_id`, or your team does not have access to it.

get.description:
Retrieves the Source connectors available to your team, including their identifier, type, name, description, and documentation link. The connectors are ordered by `connector_id`, and then by `type`. The ordering is case-sensitive, so a `connector_id` in uppercase is listed before one in lowercase.

Use the `connector_id` value returned in this response to call the [Get Configuration Details of a Source Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-sources-connectors-connector-id) endpoint and retrieve the configuration settings that the connector accepts. Connectors that your team does not have access to are not listed. A connector in beta is listed only if it has been enabled for your team.

Read [Find your Source Connector](/reference/creating-a-pipeline-with-hevo-api#step-1-find-your-source-connector) for more information about how to find the connector for your Source.

400.description:
The request is not valid. This occurs when:

- The `limit` value is not an integer, or is outside the range of 1 to 500.
- The `cursor` value was returned by a different endpoint, or the last connector in the previous response is no longer in the list. For example, you sent a different `type` value from the one in the previous request, and that connector does not ingest data from the Source type that you send in the current request.

get.summary: Get Configuration Details of a Source Connector
get.description: Retrieves the configuration settings that a Source connector accepts, including their data type, whether they are required, their default value, and the values they allow. Hevo returns these settings as a JSON schema draft 2020-12 definition, in which the settings specific to the connector are grouped under `config`. Use this schema to build the Source details that you send while [creating a Pipeline](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines), or to validate them before you send the request. The schema states the following: - A key listed under `required` must always be sent. A key that Hevo fills with a default value when it is not sent is not required. - A key that applies only under a condition, such as the credentials of a specific authentication method, is defined in an `if`/`then` block inside `allOf`, and is required only when that condition is met. - A credential is a string marked `writeOnly: true` and `format: password`. Hevo never returns credentials in any response. - A key that accepts a fixed set of values is defined as a `oneOf` list of `const` values, each with its display name in `title`. - A key that accepts a fixed set of values that the form does not show as a list is defined as an `enum`. - A key with a range, length or format rule carries the `minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength`, `maxLength` or `pattern` keyword. - Two keys that you must send together are linked by a `dependentRequired` rule in the object that holds them. - The `type` key lists the Source variants that your team can use. This key is optional. If you omit it, Hevo uses the connector’s base variant. For example, for the `SOURCE_CONNECTOR_MYSQL` connector, Hevo uses `MYSQL`, so send `AURORA` to create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Source. Refer to [Reading the Schema](/reference/creating-a-pipeline-with-hevo-api#reading-the-schema) for more information about how to read this schema and build a request from it. The schema describes only the settings that you can configure through the API. A connector that authenticates with OAuth has an `auth` object, in which you send the credentials of your own OAuth app. Hevo exchanges them for an authorization, so the Source is set up without a browser sign-in. A connector that offers a choice of authentication methods lists every one of them in its authentication method key under `config`, including the method that signs in through a browser. To set up the Source without a browser, keep or select the OAuth method and send the `auth` object. The `auth` object is not listed under the top-level `required` keyword, but a request that selects an OAuth method without sending the `auth` object is rejected. In the `auth` object, send the `client_id` and `client_secret` of your app under `client_access`, along with one of the following tokens: - `refresh_token`: A long-lived credential that Hevo exchanges for a new access token each time the current one expires. Most Sources issue a refresh token, so this is the token that most connectors require. The schema always lists both `refresh_token` and `access_token` under `auth`, in an `anyOf` block that requires at least one of them. It does not state which of the two a connector needs, so refer to the respective Source documentation for the token to send. - `access_token`: The credential that authorizes each call Hevo makes to your Source. Send this for a Source that does not issue a refresh token, such as Facebook Ads and TikTok Ads. Some connectors also require an app-level credential, such as the `developer_token` for Microsoft Ads. The schema lists it alongside `client_id` and `client_secret` under `auth.client_access`. An app credential is listed in `client_access`, but it is not included in that object’s `required` list. Send it whenever the provider needs it. Hevo does not check for it when it reads the request, but the Source connection test fails without it, and no Pipeline is created. Refer to [Authenticating SaaS Sources](/reference/authenticating-saas-sources) for more information about the credentials that each Source accepts.

get.description:
Retrieves details of all Pipelines in your workspace, including their Source and Destination details. Results are ordered oldest first. Pipelines that are being deleted, or have been deleted, are never listed. The response lists only the Pipelines in the region of the base URL that you call.

To keep the response small, this endpoint returns a summary of each Pipeline rather than its complete details. The following are not included:

- `source_schema_status`, which shows when Hevo last read the structure of the objects and fields in your Source.
- `runs`, which shows when the Pipeline last ran, when it is scheduled to run next, and whether a run is currently in progress.

To retrieve the complete details of a single Pipeline, including both of these, use the [Get Details of a Pipeline](/reference/get_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id) endpoint.

Refer to [Listing your Pipelines](/reference/managing-pipelines#listing-your-pipelines) for more information about how to list and filter your Pipelines.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value used to retrieve the next set of results. Provide the `next_cursor` value returned in the previous API response.

400.description:
The list of Pipelines could not be retrieved. This occurs when:

- The `state` value is not valid.
- A state for deleted Pipelines is specified.
- The `destination_id` value is not numeric.
- The `limit` value is not an integer, or is outside the range of 1 to 500.
- The `cursor` value cannot be decoded.

A `connector_id` or `destination_id` that matches nothing is not an error. The response is a 200 with an empty `data` array.

post.description:
Creates a Pipeline with the specified Source, Destination, and Pipeline settings.

You can create a Pipeline for any Source if you can send its credentials in the request. The credentials are of three types:

- **Static token**: The Source authenticates with a credential that does not expire, such as a Stripe API key or a HubSpot private app token. Send it in `config`.
- **Your own OAuth app**: The Source authenticates with OAuth, and you supply the credentials of an OAuth app that you own. This works for the OAuth connectors that Hevo can authorize through the API. A request that sends `auth` for a connector that does not authorize with OAuth, or for one that Hevo cannot authorize this way, returns a `400`.
- **Database credentials**: The Source is a database, such as MySQL or PostgreSQL. Send its host, port, user, password and database name in `config`.

To use your own OAuth app, send its credentials in the `auth` object. Refer to [Authenticating SaaS Sources](/reference/authenticating-saas-sources) for more information about the credentials that each Source accepts.

You cannot create a Pipeline for a Source that requires you to sign in through a browser. Such a request returns a `400`.

Replication does not start by default. The `create_disabled` value defaults to `true`, so Hevo creates the Pipeline in a disabled state. Enable it with the [Enable a Pipeline](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-actions-enable) endpoint once you are satisfied with it.

Hevo validates the whole request before it writes anything. If you send `auth`, Hevo first obtains a token. It then tests the Source and Destination connections in parallel, and waits up to five minutes for each. If a test fails, the request returns a `400` with the connector’s reason, and nothing is saved. The `200` response returns once the Pipeline is configured, before Hevo reads the Source schema. Until Hevo has read the Source schema, the object list can be empty and `source_schema_status` can be incomplete. post.description: Resyncs the specified `pipeline_id` by running the historical load again for all of its active objects. Use the `drop_and_load` parameter to specify whether Hevo drops and recreates the Destination tables before it loads the historical data again. The request body is optional, and leaving it out is the same as setting `drop_and_load` to `false`. With `false`, Hevo keeps your Destination tables, applies any schema changes to them and loads the data into them again. When you resync a Pipeline, Hevo performs the following actions: - Deletes the schedules of the Pipeline and cancels the jobs that are running. - Releases the resources that Hevo created in your Source, such as the replication slot on a PostgreSQL Source. - Reads the Source schema and the Destination schema again, and resets the object mappings. - Restores the schedule of the Pipeline. If `schedule.sync_type` is `ON_DEMAND`, the sync starts immediately. If the resync fails, the Pipeline moves to the `Failed` state. Read Resync Pipeline for more information about the actions performed on your Pipeline when you resync it. The response returns the Pipeline in the `Restarting` state, and the Pipeline reaches the `Initialized` state once the action completes. To re-ingest particular objects without resyncing the whole Pipeline, use the [Trigger Resync for a Set of Objects](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects-actions-resync) endpoint instead. Refer to [Resyncing a Pipeline](/reference/syncing-and-resyncing-pipelines#resyncing-a-pipeline) for more information about when and how to resync a Pipeline.

patch.description:
Allows you to control which Source objects are replicated in the specified `pipeline_id`. You can select all objects, exclude all objects, or retain the existing selection. You can also configure the load mode and the fields for the selected objects.

In the request body, list only the objects that you want to change. Hevo keeps the current settings of every object that you do not list, so you do not need to send the full list each time.

**Note:** If you cannot send a `PATCH` request, send the same request body to the [Manage Objects in a Pipeline (POST)](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects) endpoint.

The following rules apply to the objects that you name in the request:

- The rule for a child object depends on the group it belongs to. A child object that Hevo replicates along with its parent cannot be selected on its own, and takes the selection of its parent. You can still name such a child to change its load mode or its fields, as long as the request gives it the same selection as its parent object.
- A child object that needs its parent can be selected only while the parent stays selected after the request. Select the parent object in the same request.
- The effect on the child objects depends on the `child_selection_mode` of the parent. If it is `AUTO_FOLLOW_HEAD`, selecting or clearing the parent applies the same selection to the child objects, unless you name them yourself. If it is `REQUIRE_HEAD_SELECTED`, clearing the parent clears the child objects, and selecting the parent leaves them unselected.
- If the [List All Pipeline Objects](/reference/get_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects) endpoint does not return the `selectable` field for an object, you may not be able to name its child objects in the request. In that case, change the parent object instead, and the child objects take its selection. Such an object may also not be able to use the `MERGE` load mode if it has no primary key. Hevo applies this check only once it knows the fields of the object.
- An object that Hevo marks as not selectable cannot be selected. If the status of an object does not allow a change, remove that object from the request.
- Unless the Pipeline is disabled, the request must keep at least one object of the Pipeline selected for replication. A disabled Pipeline may be left with nothing selected.

Refer to [Managing Objects in Pipelines](/reference/managing-objects-in-pipelines) for more information about load modes, fields, and object groups.

post.description:
Allows you to control which Source objects are replicated in the specified `pipeline_id`. You can select all objects, exclude all objects, or retain the existing selection. You can also configure the load mode and the fields for the selected objects.

**Note**: Use this endpoint if you cannot send a `PATCH` request. Otherwise, use the [Manage Objects in a Pipeline (PATCH)](/reference/patch_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects) endpoint, which performs the same update.

In the request body, list only the objects that you want to change. Hevo keeps the current settings of every object that you do not list, so you do not need to send the full list each time.

The following rules apply to the objects that you name in the request:

- The rule for a child object depends on the group it belongs to. A child object that Hevo replicates along with its parent cannot be selected on its own, and takes the selection of its parent. You can still name such a child to change its load mode or its fields, as long as the request gives it the same selection as its parent object.
- A child object that needs its parent can be selected only while the parent stays selected after the request. Select the parent object in the same request.
- The effect on the child objects depends on the `child_selection_mode` of the parent. If it is `AUTO_FOLLOW_HEAD`, selecting or clearing the parent applies the same selection to the child objects, unless you name them yourself. If it is `REQUIRE_HEAD_SELECTED`, clearing the parent clears the child objects, and selecting the parent leaves them unselected.
- If the [List All Pipeline Objects](/reference/get_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects) endpoint does not return the `selectable` field for an object, you may not be able to name its child objects in the request. In that case, change the parent object instead, and the child objects take its selection. Such an object may also not be able to use the `MERGE` load mode if it has no primary key. Hevo applies this check only once it knows the fields of the object.
- An object that Hevo marks as not selectable cannot be selected. If the status of an object does not allow a change, remove that object from the request.
- Unless the Pipeline is disabled, the request must keep at least one object of the Pipeline selected for replication. A disabled Pipeline may be left with nothing selected.

Refer to [Managing Objects in Pipelines](/reference/managing-objects-in-pipelines) for more information about load modes, fields, and object groups.

202.description: Successfully updated the object selection for the specified `pipeline_id`. A Pipeline in the `Disabled` state stays `Disabled`. Any other Pipeline moves to the `Initializing` state while Hevo applies the change. To confirm that the change is applied, use the [Get Details of a Pipeline](/reference/get_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id) endpoint to check the `state` value until it is `Initialized`.

post.summary: Trigger Resync for a Set of Objects
post.description:
Re-ingests all the data for the objects that you name in the specified `pipeline_id`. The schedule, the state of the Pipeline, and every object that you do not name are left unchanged.

List the fully qualified names of the objects that you want to resync in `object_names`, up to 50 in a single request. A fully qualified name is the database, the schema and the table of the object joined by dots, leaving out any level that your Source does not have. For example, `public.orders` or `shop.public.orders`. Retrieve the names from the [List All Pipeline Objects](/reference/get_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects) endpoint. To resync every active object instead, use the [Resync a Pipeline](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-actions-resync) endpoint.

Use the `drop_and_load` parameter to specify whether Hevo drops and recreates the Destination table of each object before it loads the data again.

Refer to [Resyncing Objects](/reference/syncing-and-resyncing-pipelines#resyncing-objects) for more information about the actions performed on your objects when you resync them.

get.summary: Get Replication Position of a Pipeline
get.description:
Retrieves the replication position of each active object in the specified `pipeline_id`. Each object replicates independently, so a Pipeline has no single overall position. The response lists the objects in the `ACTIVE` status and those that are being reset. A selected object in the `BLOCKED` or `INCONSISTENT` status is not listed. The offset identifies the last point in your Source that Hevo has replicated for an object. Hevo returns the value as it reads it from your Source, and you cannot use it to restart replication from that point. Its format depends on the Source type:

- PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle return the UTC time of the last change that Hevo replicated, such as `Aug 27, 2026 13:05 UTC` for PostgreSQL and `Aug 27, 2026, 13:05 UTC` for MySQL and Oracle.
- SQL Server returns the commit and change log sequence numbers, such as `Commit LSN: 00000034:00000158:0004, Change LSN: 00000034:00000158:0003`.
- PostgreSQL in XMIN mode returns the `xmin` value on its own.
- A SaaS Source returns the keys that it tracks and their values, such as `updated_at:1756833130123`.

A value of `-` means that Hevo has not read a change for the object yet.

Hevo returns `null` as the position of an object that it has not ingested yet, and for every object in the response if the position is temporarily unavailable. The request still succeeds in both cases, so retry later. The response returns an empty list until Hevo reads the objects from your Source.

Refer to [Tracking Replication Progress](/reference/managing-objects-in-pipelines#tracking-replication-progress) for more information about how replication progress is tracked.

patch.summary: Modify Source Configuration in a Pipeline (PATCH)
patch.description:
Modifies the Source configuration for the specified `pipeline_id`. The available settings depend on the Source type.

**Note**: If you cannot send a `PATCH` request, send the same request body to the [Modify Source Configuration in a Pipeline (POST)](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-sources) endpoint.

In the request body, send only the values that you want to change, and send at least one of `name`, `config` or `auth`. Hevo keeps the current value of every field that you do not send. The `config` object holds the Source configuration fields for the connector, and you can send only the fields that the connector allows you to edit. Hevo rejects a field that cannot be edited even when the value you send is the same as the stored one.

To clear the value of a field, send that field as `null`. The connector then applies its default value for the field. A key that is not a field of the connector is not rejected and is stored as it is, so check your field names against the connector schema.

For a database Source, you can change only some fields, such as the password and the SSH tunnel and SSL settings. Refer to [Changing a Source](/reference/modifying-the-source-configuration#changing-a-source) for the fields that you can change.

Hevo validates the change and runs a Source connection test before it saves the change, but only when the request changes `config` or sends `auth`. A change to only the name is not tested. A configuration that the Source rejects returns a `400` with the reason, and nothing is saved. The Pipeline stays in its current state, because the Source is edited on its own. A test that is still running after five minutes returns a `500`.

To rotate the credentials of an OAuth Source without a browser sign-in, send the `auth` object with the following:

- The `client_id` and `client_secret` of your own OAuth app, under `client_access`.
- Any app-level credential that the provider requires.
- A `refresh_token` or an `access_token`.

Hevo exchanges them for a new token and tests it before it saves the change, so credentials that do not work leave the Source unchanged. If the test fails, Hevo revokes the new token. If the change succeeds, Hevo does not revoke the token that it replaces.

Sending `auth` for a connector that does not support OAuth, or for one that Hevo cannot authorize through the API, returns a `400`, and Hevo rejects the whole request, including any `config` change in it. Update a connector that does not use OAuth through `config`, for example by sending a new `database_password`, and authorize the other kind in the Hevo UI. Credentials are never returned, so the response includes no Source configuration.

The following changes cancel the current authorization, so send `auth` in the same request:

- A change to `config.authentication_method`, even to a method that does not use OAuth.
- A change to a field that the provider uses to build the OAuth connection, such as a Salesforce account type or a Zendesk domain.

Sending `auth` rotates the credentials of an OAuth Source that Hevo can authorize through the API, whether it was authorized in the Hevo UI or through the API. No confirmation is needed.

Refer to [Changing a Source](/reference/modifying-the-source-configuration#changing-a-source) for more information about the steps to change the Source settings and rotate its credentials.

400.description:
The Source configuration could not be modified. This occurs when:

- The request body changes nothing.
- The request body includes a blank `name`, or a name that is already in use.
- The request body names a field that the connector does not support editing.
- The Source connection test fails.
- The credentials of your own OAuth app are incomplete, or the provider rejects them.
- The request changes `config.authentication_method`, or a field that the provider uses to build the OAuth connection, without sending `auth` in the same request.
- The Pipeline is in the `Failed` state.
- The request has no body.

Configuration settings that you want to change. Hevo updates the settings you send, and the settings you leave out keep their stored values. Read the settings that your connector accepts from the [Get Configuration Details of a Destination Connector](/reference/get_api-v2-metadata-destinations-connectors-connector-id) endpoint. Some settings cannot be changed after the Destination is created. A request that sends such a setting is rejected with a `400` that names it, and nothing is saved.

Determines the objects selected for replication in the Pipeline. This field is optional and defaults to `RETAIN_EXISTING`. Its value is not case-sensitive.

Any other value returns a `400`.

x-enumDescriptions.INCLUDE_ALL: Selects all Source objects for replication except the ones you exclude.
x-enumDescriptions.EXCLUDE_ALL: Excludes all Source objects except the ones you include.
x-enumDescriptions.RETAIN_EXISTING: Keeps the current selection without changing which objects are replicated.

objects.description: List of the objects that you want to change. List each object only once. This field is required when `selection_mode` is `RETAIN_EXISTING`, and it must then hold at least one object. With `INCLUDE_ALL` or `EXCLUDE_ALL`, you can leave this list out or send it empty.

load_mode.description: Mode in which you want to load data from the Source object into the Destination table. If you do not send this value, the object continues to use its current load mode. The value is case-sensitive. Hevo ignores it when `selected` is `false`, and `OVERWRITE` is never accepted here. The object must allow the mode you send, and some objects do not allow the mode to be changed at all. A value that the object does not allow returns a `400`.

x-enumDescriptions.MERGE: Existing records are updated based on matching criteria, such as primary keys, and new records are added to your Destination table if no match is found.
x-enumDescriptions.APPEND: New records are added at the end of your Destination table without modifying or deleting any existing data.
x-enumDescriptions.HISTORY_TRACKING: Every version of a record is retained in your Destination table as the record changes in the Source. Each change is added as a new row, alongside timestamps that define the period during which that version was valid.

include_fields.description: List of fields that you want to include for replication. This list changes the current field selection. A field that you do not name keeps the state it has.

exclude_fields.description:
List of fields that you want to exclude from replication. This list changes the current field selection. A field that you do not name keeps the state it has.

The following rules apply to both field lists. Hevo rejects a request that breaks any of them, and nothing is saved.

- You cannot send these lists when `selected` is `false`.
- A field cannot appear in both lists, or twice in the same list, and a name cannot be blank.
- Hevo removes leading and trailing spaces and then matches the name exactly, so the name is case-sensitive. A name that is not a field of the object is rejected, and the message lists the names you can use.
- You cannot exclude a field that Hevo marks as a key of the object. With the `MERGE` load mode, the primary key cannot be excluded.
- Unless the Pipeline is disabled, at least one field of the object must stay selected.

A name that you repeat is resynced once. Hevo removes leading and trailing spaces from each name.
